observed_title: Generalisation of Farkas’ lemma beyond closedness: a constructive approach via Fenchel-Rockafellar duality

read_ranges.scope: Sequential complete reading1–370,371–740,741–1110,1111–1486, including all introductory statements, Sections2–4, infinite-dimensional and finite-dimensional counterexamples, AppendixA LemmasA.1–A.4 proofs on pages25–27, and all references to final page29. Rendered original PDF pages5,6,7,10,12,16,21,22,24,26,27: distinguish image closures and closed convex hull overbars, inspect gauge/support identities, ball-normal uniqueness, shared-normal reconstruction, cone counterexample and appendix formulas.

topic_relevance.B01: direct: separates closure membership/approximate solvability from exact cone-constrained linear solvability using a common finite constant and constructive dual variables.
topic_relevance.B04: direct: primal attainment, dual attainment, shared normals, closed adjoint range and extra positivity; does not supply a general minimax exchange.
topic_relevance.A03: adjacent: Hilbert weak compactness and escaping/gauge-unbounded approximations; does not give center-cube compactness.

definitions.name: Hilbert model and cone generator
definitions.statement: X,Y are real Hilbert spaces and A∈L(X,Y) is bounded linear, with Hilbert adjoint A*. K_r is bounded, norm-closed, convex and contains0; P_r=cone(K_r) may be nonclosed. A cone contains0 and is stable under nonnegative scaling.

definitions.name: Approximate versus exact solvability
definitions.statement: Approximate means ∀ε>0 ∃x_ε∈P_r with||Ax_ε−b||≤ε, equivalently b∈cl A(P_r); exact means ∃x∈P_r withAx=b, equivalently b∈A(P_r). Extracted text loses overbars; original PDF5–6 confirms closure in Theorems1.2(i),1.3(i).

definitions.name: Polar, gauge and support
definitions.statement: P_r^∘={z:⟨z,x⟩≤0 ∀x∈P_r}. j_K(x)=inf{α>0:x∈αK}; σ_K(z)=sup_{v∈K}⟨z,v⟩≥0. Boundedness gives a finite Lipschitz support with constantR_K=sup_K||v||. Gauge domain=coneK and gauge zero only at0.

definitions.name: Auxiliary primal and dual
definitions.statement: P_ε minimizesF_ε(x)=1/2 j_K(x)^2+δ_{B(b,ε)}(Ax). D_ε minimizesJ_ε(y)=1/2 σ_K(A*y)^2−⟨b,y⟩+ε||y||. Value relation isπ_ε=−infJ_ε. Both are minimizations with opposite values; D_ε is not the original primal’s linear objective.

definitions.name: Single-valued and extremal recovery conditions
definitions.statement: H: Ran(A*)⊆P_r^∘∪sing(K_r)^c, where sing means the support maximizer face is not a singleton. For nonconvex coneP=coneK, useK_r=cl convK andE:ext(K_r)⊆K. These are additional assumptions. H may be checked at the actual dual minimizer instead of globally when only that recovery is claimed.

本次核验：best constant isinf{j_K(x):Ax=b}=sqrt(2π_0), achieved as gauge minimum when feasible. Atb=0 the best infimum is0; theorem usesC>0, so0 is an infimum of admissible positive constants.

The general Hilbert proof depends on Fenchel-Rockafellar and weak compactness; the suggested Banach extensions inSection1.5 are prospects, not proved results.

theorem_cards.label: Proposition2.1 / AppendixA.1–A.2: auxiliary strong duality and primal attainment
assumptions: K bounded closed convex containing0 in a Hilbert space.
A bounded linear andε≥0; infeasible primal is allowed as extendedπ_ε=∞.
theorem_cards.statement: π_ε=−infJ_ε for everyε≥0; ifπ_ε is finite, the primal minimum is attained. j_K and1/2j_K² are proper convex lsc; conjugate(1/2j_K²)*=1/2σ_K² is finite continuous everywhere. This proves primal attainment, not automatic exact-dual attainment.
proof_steps: 作者证明：AppendixA.1 uses boundedness/closedness for attained radial gauge; AppendixA.2 proves lsc using weak compactness ofK and squared-gauge/support conjugacy through a scalar composition formula (lines1293–1350).
作者证明：F*=1/2σ_K² continuous everywhere andG*=⟨b,·⟩+ε||·|| finite everywhere satisfy dual-side Fenchel-Rockafellar qualification, giving equal values and finite primal attainment (lines645–652).

本次核验：ifR_K>0,||x||≤R_K j_K(x); gauge sublevel sets lie inαK and are weakly compact, supporting finite-primal attainment. K={0} is a separate degenerate feasible caseb near0 and is not handled by dividing byR_K.
gaps: Appendix conjugate composition and Fenchel-Rockafellar are cited dependencies, not independently proved in full here.
The printed AppendixA.2 lsc proof writesj_K(x)=λ afterx=λv,v∈K; onlyj_K(x)≤λ is needed and generally follows. This local inequality correction preserves lsc.

theorem_cards.label: Theorems1.4–1.5 / Proposition3.2 / Lemma3.5: approximate uniqueness and exact reconstruction
assumptions: Exact branch:b∈A(P_r),ε=0; recovery fromy* additionally requires an attainedD_0 minimizer.
theorem_cards.statement: Forε>0, primal minimizers exist and the dual minimizer is unique. General gauge primal minimizers need not be unique, but all have the same imageAx*. For a closed cone, norm² primal is uniquely minimized andx*=(A*y*)_+. Atε=0, primal still attains; D_0 may be nonunique or fail to attain. With an attained dual, x*∈σ_K(A*y*)∂σ_K(A*y*).
proof_steps: 作者证明：J_ε coercivity uses normalized unbounded minimizing candidates, weak subsequence and the zero-support implication (lines735–762).

作者证明：if||b||≤ε, primalx*=0 and dualy*=0; if||b||>ε, all optimalimages lie on theε-sphere and convexity forces the image to a singleton. Normal cone forces ally* onto one ray; the quadratic along that ray has a unique minimizer (lines806–838).

本次核验补足：at||b||=ε>0,σ_K(A*b)>0 follows from approximate-solvability implication: support0 would give||b||²≤0. Thus the ray quadratic has strictly positive quadratic coefficient, justifying the printed “clear” uniqueness step.
作者证明：forclosedP,Moreau givesσ_K(z)=||z_+|| andσ_K(z)∂σ_K(z)={z_+}; strictnorm² gives unique primal (lines892–920).
gaps: General inclusion is necessary for an optimal pair, but selecting an arbitrary member of a nonsingleton support face need not preserveAx=b or residual≤ε. Full saddle system includesy*∈−N_{B(b,ε)}(Ax*).
ε→0 does not imply dual attainment or bounded primal/dual candidates.
No rate for optimization ofJ_ε, discretization error or iteration complexity is proved.

theorem_cards.label: Proposition1.1 / Theorem1.6 / Corollary1.1: recovery to the original nonconvex cone
assumptions: P anycone generated by boundedK containing0;K_r=closed convex hullK,P_r=coneK_r.
H ensures support product singleton; E says extreme points ofK_r belong toK.
Approximate: b∈cl A(P_r),ε>0; exact: b∈A(P_r) plus attainedD_0.
theorem_cards.statement: UnderH the support product uniquely identifies the optimalprimal. UnderH–E it belongs to the originalP, so approximate solutions recover inP and exact solutions recover inP whenD_0 attains. Corollary1.1 statescl A(P_r)=cl A(P), with overbars onbothsides; it does not assert unconditional exact-image equality.
proof_steps: 作者证明：support maximizers form a nonempty exposed face by weakcompactness; H makes it singleton unlesssupport0,whose scaled product is{0}. Unique maximizer isextreme;Eplacesit inK, andmultiplication staysinconeK (lines933–964).
本次核验：PDF10 confirms closures inCorollary1.1. Exactpart requires dualattainment before usingthe reconstructedvariable.
gaps: No automatic recovery follows from convexification alone.
H–E are structural assumptions, not numerical single-maximizer observations at finitelymany directions.
Finite-dimensionalstrongcompactK_r and closedK, or weaklyclosedK, are stated sufficient routes forE viaMilman; that theorem is external.
